skill.name: python-web-app-security-audit
skill.description: Run configurable, defensive pytest checks against Python ASGI applications before release, with evidence-based findings and documented test boundaries.
skill.summary: Audit Python web application controls with a configurable in-process pytest suite.
skill.author: glenskii

security_audit.summary: The 126 static findings are false positives caused by defensive test payloads, local configuration, in-process HTTP clients, documentation, and bounded file copying. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or hidden command execution was found. Active registration and rate-limit tests still present a medium operational risk outside an isolated test environment.

remediation.issue: State-changing and burst tests can affect shared application data or account defenses.
remediation.suggestion: Require an explicit test-environment confirmation before collection, and provide opt-in markers for registration and high-volume rate-limit tests.

remediation.issue: The registration test can create a persistent account when the endpoint accepts the request.
remediation.suggestion: Create unique test identities through a fixture and remove created records during teardown.

content.user_title: Audit Python Web Applications Before Release
content.value_statement: Security regressions can hide across authentication, authorization, headers, and configuration. This skill runs configurable pytest checks and produces evidence-based release findings.
actual_capabilities: Copies a bundled pytest security suite into a target project without overwriting an existing security directory.
Loads configurable ASGI applications for in-process testing across FastAPI, Django, Flask adapters, and similar services.
Tests authentication, authorization, CORS, cookies, headers, rate limits, validation, errors, methods, and configuration.
Uses configurable routes, origins, thresholds, and dedicated test credentials from a local test environment file.
Produces findings with evidence, severity, remediation, boundaries, and a release decision.
limitations: The suite does not replace penetration testing, dependency scanning, or infrastructure review.
It cannot verify production TLS, reverse proxies, WAF controls, external identity providers, or unconfigured routes.
Default routes and assertions require adaptation to each application's behavior and authentication format.
State-changing and burst tests can affect data or rate limits without an isolated test environment.

use_cases.title: Harden an ASGI Service
use_cases.description: Adapt and run defensive checks before merging a FastAPI, Django, or Flask application release.

use_cases.title: Review Security Controls
use_cases.description: Verify authentication, authorization, validation, browser protections, and error handling with repeatable application tests.

use_cases.title: Support Release Decisions
use_cases.description: Turn test evidence, skipped controls, and residual boundaries into a clear release recommendation.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare the Suite
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare the bundled suite for this ASGI project. Identify required dependencies, configuration values, and safe test boundaries before running tests.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a local project

prompt_templates.title: Adapt Application Routes
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt routes and authentication fixtures for this Django ASGI application. Use dedicated test accounts and explain every skipped check.

prompt_templates.title: Triage Test Failures
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the configured security suite, triage failures, and separate verified vulnerabilities from route mismatches or unsupported controls.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Release Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess release readiness from these results. Correlate authentication, authorization, validation, and configuration evidence, then document residual risk and remediation priorities.

output_examples.input: A FastAPI project needs pre-release security checks.
output: The suite is configured for the local ASGI application and dedicated test accounts.
Authentication, authorization, headers, CORS, cookies, validation, errors, and rate limits are tested.
The report separates verified findings from skipped infrastructure controls.

output_examples.input: The authorization suite returns unexpected 404 responses.
output_examples.output: The configured IDOR route does not exist. Update the route template before treating these responses as authorization evidence.

output_examples.input: The full suite passes with several skipped infrastructure checks.
output_examples.output: Release decision: review required. Application checks passed, but skipped infrastructure controls need separate evidence and an owner decision.

best_practices: Run the suite against an isolated application, test database, and dedicated accounts.
Configure real routes and expected controls before interpreting failures or skips.
Record application revision, environment, command, evidence, boundaries, and retest results.
anti_patterns: Do not run state-changing or burst tests against production systems.
Do not treat default-route 404 responses as confirmed vulnerabilities.
Do not present a passing suite as a penetration test or complete security proof.

faq.question: Which Python frameworks are supported?
faq.answer: FastAPI works directly. Django needs an ASGI entry point, and Flask needs a maintained ASGI adapter.

faq.question: Does the suite open a public server?
faq.answer: No. httpx ASGITransport exercises the imported application in process.

faq.question: Can I use production credentials?
faq.answer: No. Use dedicated test accounts and keep the local test environment file out of version control.

faq.question: Does a passing run prove the application is secure?
faq.answer: No. It covers configured application behavior and does not replace broader manual, dependency, or infrastructure assessment.

faq.question: How should skipped tests be reported?
faq.answer: Record why each test was skipped, whether the control applies, and which separate evidence covers it.

faq.question: Can the tests change application state?
faq.answer: Yes. Registration and rate-limit tests can create records or affect controls, so use an isolated test environment.
